Live: Tamil Nadu in contempt for not lighting Deepathoon lamp, ASI tells SCMadurai Deepathoon Row Live Updates: The Supreme Court hearing in the Deepam row case began on Friday, with senior advocate J Sai Deepak appearing for the Hindu Dharma Parishad and senior advocate Gopa Sankaranarayanan representing the Madurai Collector. At the outset, the Supreme Court clarified that it would not examine the larger dispute and would restrict the hearing to the alleged non-compliance with its November 20, order permitting the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon pillar. Today's hearing comes two days after the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the Supreme Court over the failure to light the lamp at Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities. The controversy escalated after the annual Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary location, the Uchipillayar mandapam, on Monday, and not at the disputed stone pillar, despite the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the ritual at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time measure. Live: Reddy's YSRCP likely to back Delimitation Bill, BRS offers conditional supportUnion Cabinet Meeting Live Updates: Jagan Mohan Reddy's YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to back the Delimitation Bill, with the party expected to take a formal decision on Friday, sources told India Today. The development comes as the Union Cabinet is likely to consider two major delimitation reforms, including a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats across all states and a proposal to delink the exercise from the Census. The meeting comes ahead of special sittings of Parliament, amid indications that the government may reintroduce a constitutional amendment linking women's reservation to delimitation. Meanwhile, the Congress and NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) have asked all their MPs to remain present during the special sittings. The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with proceedings scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
